messages:
Aisha: quick heads-up, ran a targeted perf sweep today for Qwen->Mix_draft routing, found a few small but compounding regressions
Tom: ok, summary?
Aisha: short prompts (<=64 tokens) p99 up ~12-28% and speculative accept_rate down ~13% when routing Qwen traffic to Mix_draft variants
Diego: sounds bad. what are the suspects?
Aisha: multiple interacting causes:
Aisha: - kernel selector falls back to generic GEMM when head_dim mismatch occurs (Qwen=128 vs Mix_draft=96) -> ~+1.0-2.2ms/token cost
Aisha: - tokenizer boundary differences: Mix_draft splits frequent suffixes differently, lowering draft logits and increasing spec rejections
Aisha: - KV cache churn: mixed-family batching triggers per-variant reinitialization (reinit_store) adding ~3-6ms at burst start
Priya: can we see profiler snippet?
Aisha: here's a trimmed perf-trace:
Aisha: ```
Aisha: trace: route=Qwen->Mix_draft seq=32
Aisha: kernel_select: generic_gemm fallback 46% samples
Aisha: kv_ops: reinit_store 29% samples, avg_extra=4.0ms
Aisha: decode_speculative: accept_rate=0.59 (same-family baseline ~0.83)
Aisha: overall_p99_delta=+18%
Aisha: ```
Tom: ok so small things adding up. Why strict kernel key?
Aisha: selector keys are exact (head_dim, kv_dim, dtype). No fuzzy match. If head_dim differs, we fallback. Proposal: introduce kernel compatibility buckets (e.g., {64,96}, {128,256}) and allow selector to choose nearest kernel when microbench shows <5% overhead
Diego: correctness risk if layouts/padding differ. But we can limit to divisibility-aligned dims and add a perf/correctness microbench before enabling mapping
Priya: short-term tokenizer mitigation?
Aisha: prototype a router-side tokenizer normalization map for top N suffix/prefix differences and normalize logits used for draft acceptance. Canary improved spec_accept ~+7%
Diego: longer-term: prefer pairing variants that share canonical tokenizer or run a tiny tokenizer-sim score at routing time and avoid low-sim pairs
Tom: KV warmup mitigation options?
Aisha: two approaches considered:
Aisha: - sticky-allocator: group by model-family inside a small batching window to avoid interleaved reinit (adds <=1ms scheduling jitter)
Aisha: - lazy-kv-init: postpone per-request KV init until after handshake to avoid wasted stores for dropped drafts
Tom: sticky scheduling seems fine if jitter bounded and opt-in per route
Aisha: acceptance threshold tuning: raising spec_accept threshold from 0.60->0.72 reduced retry loops but allowed occasional lower-quality accepts. Must gate via eval set
Diego: we need automated daily eval per route and alerts if quality drops >2% after threshold changes
Aisha: action items added:
Aisha: 1) kernel-catalog: add compat buckets + microbench harness (owner: Diego)
Aisha: 2) tokenizer-normalization map prototype + route-sim tests (owner: Priya)
Aisha: 3) kv-strategy: implement sticky-allocator opt-in + perf guardrail (owner: Tom)
Aisha: 4) acceptance SLOs: daily eval + alerting pipeline (owner: Aisha)
Tom: add metrics: kernel_fallback_rate and kernel_mismatch_p99 per model-pair
Priya: will push tokenizer diff tonight with token examples
perf-bot: nightly-summary job=nightly-sweep-1934566000 route=Qwen->Mix_draft samples=2.3k p95=40ms(+12%) p99=73ms(+19%) spec_accept=0.59 action=investigate
InfraBot: deploy-checklist created: feature-flag sticky-allocator, perf-gate=+3% throughput degradation
Diego: I'll start microbench harness and post candidate numbers EOD tomorrow
Aisha: I'll draft RFC for kernel buckets + compat_ignore_head_padding flag for edge cases and wire daily eval hooks for acceptance changes
Tom: SGTM. Keep thread for short updates; reopen if new regression appears
Priya: noted, thanks all :thumbsup:
